title: auspol canonical dataset
description: Single source of truth for the auspol tracker. Edit this file to add a poll, then run: node .build/newtracker/build.mjs (which validates before it builds).

metricRules.description: Which question a house asks about a leader. Approval = approve minus disapprove; favourability = positive minus negative. Never blended, because they are different questions.

favFirms.description: Canonical lower-case firm names that publish favourability for every leader.

overrides.description: Keyed 'firm|leaderKey'. Date-bounded, because what a house asks can change mid-cycle.

pollsterRules.description: House facts the build must know about: a deliberate oddity the validator would otherwise report every run, and a release schedule that is known rather than inferred.

tppIncludesUndecided.description: The house's published 2PP pair sums to under 100 because undecideds are included.

release.description: A DECLARED publication schedule, for a house whose rhythm is known but whose recorded releases do not measure it - too few of them, or dated from something other than the post. It overrides the measured habit in "Next expected polls" and is labelled there as stated rather than measured, so a reader can tell the two apart. Delete it once enough `published` values exist to measure the same thing.

dow.description: Weekday the house publishes on, 0 = Sunday, matching Date#getDay().

time.description: Hour it files, 24-hour, eastern - the same frame as a `published` clock time.

note.description: Where the claim comes from, and why the measurement is not trusted instead.

stopped.description: The house has stopped publishing, declared by hand. It drops the house out of "Next expected polls" entirely - a silent house otherwise KEEPS its slot there, marked overdue, until a release is recorded, so there is no other way a dead house leaves the list. Delete the flag if it resumes.

skippedSlots.description: Release-slot dates (YYYY-MM-DD) that are confirmed absent at the publisher, written by the house's skip-confirm agent (e.g. .build/essential-confirm-skip.mjs) after it has checked the publisher index the morning after a slot passed. Each entry rolls the house's "Next expected polls" slot one cadence on, so a skipped slot stops showing as (or N days ago) instead of hanging around waiting for a release that was verified not to exist. Observational, not declared-by-hand: do not add entries without the agent's evidence checks.

elections.description: Keyed e2010, e2013, ... Each holds the election-day result used as a series baseline.

events.description: Cycle events annotated on the charts.

direction.description: Right-direction / wrong-track readings, one row per poll wave. unsure is the remainder and the three must sum to 100.

date.description: Fieldwork END date. Essential publishes by report date — re-key it onto the matching wave's fieldwork end.

polls.description: Voting-intention polls, oldest first. One row per published national poll, plus the election baseline (isElection).

date.description: Fieldwork END date (ISO). The join key for every other dataset, together with pollster.

client.description: Commissioning outlet. Resolve = 'SMH / Age', Newspoll = 'The Australian', YouGov = 'Sky News', Roy Morgan = '—'.

published.description: ISO date the poll was PUBLISHED, read off the cited source (a release header, an article's published_time). Distinct from `date`, which is the last day of fieldwork - the two differ by a day or more for most houses. Optional: where it isn't recorded the table falls back to the fieldwork end and says so. May carry a clock time as '2026-07-15T05:00' (house local time, i.e. eastern). Both halves are used: the date measures the house's publication lag, and enough timed releases let "Next expected polls" state the hour it files as well as the day. Never hand the whole string to Date.parse beside a bare date - a datetime parses as local and a date as UTC.

undecided.description: Share who can't say who they'd vote for, where the house publishes one. It sits BESIDE the primaries, not inside them - Roy Morgan sets these electors aside before reporting shares, which is why its shares still sum to 100. Record only a figure the release prints for THAT wave: a combined release covering several waves prints one figure belonging to no single wave, and those rows carry none.

ind.description: Some houses (Roy Morgan) publish one combined Independent/Other figure — put it here and leave oth null.

tpp_alp.description: Headline 2PP. Null where the house published none (Newspoll and Resolve often do not). For Roy Morgan store the RESPONDENT-ALLOCATED figure; the pair allocated on 2025-election preference flows goes in tpp_flows.

tpp_flows.description: Roy Morgan only: ALP's 2PP share allocated on the preference flows of the 2025 Federal Election — the second 2PP Roy Morgan prints beside the respondent-allocated one in tpp_alp. The ALP share is stored alone; the L-NP share is its complement. Absent, not zero: early releases print no flows pair, and a combined release's single figure belongs to no single wave — both conventions match `undecided`.

url.description: The published release this row was taken from. Link the article, not a paywall wrapper.

releaseUrl.description: The pollster's OWN release page for this wave, when it lives somewhere other than `url`. RedBridge / Accent's waves are the worked example: `url` cites the AFR article the row was read from, `releaseUrl` points at the wave's page on accent-research.com. Same deal for YouGov / News24: `url` cites the media write-up, `releaseUrl` the wave's self-release on yougov.com (released occasionally, not every wave). Optional, absent-not-zero: a wave with no pollster release page simply omits it (some old waves never had one; Accent's sitemap can lag a wave's publication by days). The expanded poll shows it as 'Pollster's release'.

assimilated.description: Row was added by an updater's assimilator from the house's own published dataset (see .build/assimilate-*.mjs), not hand-curated from a release. Such rows carry sample:null and no url — the feeds don't publish either — and are exempt from the sample-size check. Any later hand-edit that fills in the missing metadata should drop the flag with them.

sumNote.description: Documents a deliberate reason this row's shares do not sum to ~100. Presence exempts the row from the sum checks, so only use it for an adjudicated case.

ppm.description: Preferred prime minister. alb vs opp is the main contest; han only in a genuine three-way.

oppName.description: Opposition leader at the time — Ley before the 12 Feb 2026 handover, Taylor after.

han.description: Hanson's share in a THREE-way question only. A two-way Alb-v-Hanson goes in ppmHeadToHead.

extra.description: Additional contests polled the same wave.

approval.description: Leader net ratings. Each net is that leader's PRIMARY metric at that firm (see metricRules).

detail.description: Optional. { alb|opp|han: {app,dis} } = the published split behind the primary net — always record it when the pollster gave one. { fav: {...} } = a SECOND measure, when a firm published both for one leader.

ppmHeadToHead.description: Two-way Albanese-v-Hanson preferred-PM matchups, kept apart from the main contest because a two-way share is not comparable with a three-way one.

altTpp.description: Two-party head-to-heads other than ALP v L/NP.

lnpVsOnp_lnp.description: Coalition's share against One Nation. Null where the house did not ask it (Roy Morgan does not).

cyclePolls.description: Past-cycle voting intention, keyed by the year of the election that ENDED the term. Frozen history; not hand-edited.

cycleApproval.description: Past-cycle leader ratings, keyed by the year the term BEGAN. One row per wave that rated the leaders. Rows may name their metric; absent, metricRules decides. Preferred PM rides on the same row because it is the same wave asking a second question — a wave that published one and not the other simply leaves the other pair null.

pmPpm.description: Preferred-PM share for the sitting PM. Shares only — the uncommitted remainder is not stored, matching ppm[] for the current term. No past cycle is charted on this yet; it is stored so one can be.

oppPpm.description: Preferred-PM share for the opposition leader.
